items.q: Pip’s die has 8 sides. How many of its faces show an even number?
items.why: 2, 4, 6 and 8 are even. That is {answer} of the 8 faces.

items.q: Pip rolls two 4-sided dice and adds them. How many ways can he make {t}?
items.why: There are {answer} ways to make {t}. Each square in the picture is one way the two dice can land.

items.q: A spinner has 8 equal parts: 3 red, 4 blue and 1 gold. What is the chance it lands on blue?
items.why: 4 of the 8 parts are blue, so the chance is {answer}. That is the same as 1 in 2.

items.q: A trick die has the faces 1, 1, 2, 2, 2 and 6. What is the chance of rolling a 2?
items.why: Three of its six faces show a 2, so the chance is {answer}.

items.q: Coco flipped a coin and got heads 5 times in a row! On the next flip, which is more likely?
items.why: Coins have no memory. Heads and tails are always 1 in 2 each, whatever happened before.

items.q: A bag holds {r} red and {b} blue marbles. Mika takes one without looking. What is the chance it is red?
items.why: There are {r} red marbles out of {total} in all, so the chance is {answer}.

items.q: Flip 2 coins. What is the chance of one heads and one tails? Give the simplest answer.
items.why: Heads-tails and tails-heads: 2 of the 4 ways. 2 in 4 is the same as {answer}.

items.q: Roll two dice and add them. What is the chance of exactly {t}?
items.why: {t} can be made {fav} ways out of {total}, so the chance is {answer}.

items.q: Flip 4 coins. How many different ways can they land?
items.why: Each coin doubles the ways: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = {answer}.

items.q: Roll two dice. How many of the 36 ways have BOTH dice even?
items.why: Each die has 3 even faces: 2, 4 and 6. 3 × 3 = {answer} squares.

items.q: A mob rolls 1 die and ties go to you. When are you MORE likely to get hit?

labels: When you roll 2 dice and keep the best

items.why: With 2 dice you keep the best one, so the mob has to beat your best roll. That is much harder.

items.q: Roll two dice. How many of the 36 ways are the two numbers exactly {k} apart?
items.why: Count the lit squares: {answer} ways. They sit in two lines beside the doubles.

items.q: Bo rolls two dice. The first one shows {f}. What is the chance the total is 8 or more?
items.why: Once the first die shows {f}, only the 6 squares in its row count. {fav} of them make 8 or more.

items.q: Luna rolls two dice {n} times. About how many times should she get doubles?
items.why: Doubles come up 6 ways out of 36, which is 1 in 6. {n} ÷ 6 = {answer}.

items.q: Two dice. Which is more likely: a total of {x}, or doubles?
items.why: A total of {x} can be made {a_fav} ways. Doubles can be made {b_fav} ways.

items.q: Roll one die. What is the chance of a number bigger than {k}? Give the simplest answer.
items.why: {fav} faces out of 6 are bigger than {k}. {fav} in 6 is the same as {answer}.

items.q: Flip 3 coins. What is the chance of exactly 2 heads?
items.why: HHT, HTH and THH: {fav} of the {total} ways.

items.q: Pip rolls a 12-sided die. How many of its faces are a multiple of {k}?
items.why: Count them on the die: {answer} faces.

items.q: Flip 4 coins. How many of the 16 ways give exactly 2 heads?
items.why: HHTT, HTHT, HTTH, THHT, THTH and TTHH. That is {answer} ways.

items.q: Roll two dice and add them. What is the chance the total is ODD? Give the simplest answer.
items.why: Exactly half the squares, 18 of the 36, have an odd total. That is {answer}.

items.q: Roll two dice. What is the chance of doubles? Give the simplest answer.
items.why: 6 doubles out of 36 squares. 6 in 36 is the same as {answer}.

items.q: Roll one die again and again, many times. What is the average roll?
items.why: Add all the faces: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21. Then 21 ÷ 6 = {answer}.

items.q: You and a mob each roll one die. Ties go to you. What is the chance the mob hits you?
items.why: 6 squares are ties, and ties are yours. The other 30 split in half, so the mob wins {fav} of the 36.

items.q: Roll 3 dice. How many of the 216 ways have no 6 at all?
items.why: Each die has 5 faces that are not a 6. 5 × 5 × 5 = {answer}.

items.q: Roll two dice and MULTIPLY the numbers. How many of the 36 ways give an even answer?
items.why: The answer is only odd when both dice are odd: 3 × 3 = 9 ways. So 36 − 9 = {answer} ways are even.

items.q: A spinner has 10 equal parts: 5 green, 3 red and 2 blue. Spin it twice. How many of the 100 ways land on green both times?
items.why: 5 green parts the first time and 5 the second time: 5 × 5 = {answer}.

items.q: Die A has the faces 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Die B has 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4. Which one rolls a bigger number on average?
items.why: {detail} Die B never rolls very high or very low, but its average is just the same.

items.q: The mob has lots of hearts. Jab hits on a 2 or more for {j}. Smash hits on a 5 or more for {s}. Which does more damage on average?
items.why: Multiply the damage by the chance. {detail}

items.q: Coco flips 3 coins in each game. In {n} games, about how many times will all three coins match?
items.why: All heads or all tails is 2 of the 8 ways, which is 1 in 4. {n} ÷ 4 = {answer}.

items.q: The mob has {hp} hearts left. Jab: one die, a 2 or more hits for 3. Twin Strike: two dice, each 4 or more hits for 3. Which is more likely to finish the mob THIS turn?
items.why: Chance to do at least {hp} damage. {detail}

items.q: Roll 3 dice and add them. How many of the 216 ways make a total of {t}?
items.why: Only {answer}. Totals near the smallest and the biggest are rare, because there are few ways to make them.

items.q: Roll two dice and add them. How many of the 36 ways give a prime number? (The primes here are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11.)
items.why: 2 has 1 way, 3 has 2, 5 has 4, 7 has 6 and 11 has 2. Together that is {answer}.

items.q: Flip 4 coins. What is the chance of at least 3 heads?
items.why: Exactly 3 heads can happen 4 ways, and 4 heads 1 way. That makes {answer}.

items.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue marbles. Mika takes one, keeps it out, then takes another. What is the chance both are red?
items.why: First pick: 3 red out of 5. Second pick: 2 red left out of 4. 3 × 2 = 6 and 5 × 4 = 20, so the chance is {answer}.

items.q: At a fair you pay 1 coin to roll one die. If you roll a 6 you win {w} coins. Is it a good deal?
items.why: A 6 comes up 1 time in 6. {detail}

items.q: The Red die has six 3s. The Blue die has 2, 2, 2, 2, 6, 6. You roll both. Which die wins more often?
items.why: Red wins whenever Blue shows a 2. That is {a_fav} of the {total} ways.

items.q: The Blue die has 2, 2, 2, 2, 6, 6. The Green die has 1, 1, 5, 5, 5, 5. You roll both. Which die wins more often?
items.why: Blue wins {a_fav} ways and Green wins {b_fav} ways, out of {total}.

items.q: Red (all 3s) beats Blue (2, 2, 2, 2, 6, 6). Blue beats Green (1, 1, 5, 5, 5, 5). So which wins between Red and Green?
items.why: Surprise! Green wins {b_fav} of the {total} ways. These dice go round in a circle, like rock, paper, scissors.

items.q: Roll 3 dice. What is the chance of at least one 6?
items.why: No 6 at all happens 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 ways. So 216 − 125 = {fav} ways have a 6.

items.q: A mob rolls 1 die. You roll 2 dice and keep the best one. Ties go to you. What is the chance the mob hits you?
items.why: The mob must beat your best die. A mob roll of 2 beats 1 way, 3 beats 4 ways, 4 beats 9, 5 beats 16 and 6 beats 25. 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 = {fav}.

items.q: A mob with 1 die attacks you 216 times. You dodge with 2 dice and keep the best. Ties go to you. About how many attacks hit?
items.why: The mob hits 55 ways out of 216. So in 216 attacks, about {answer} hit.

items.q: Two dice roll behind a screen. Zip peeks and says: at least one of them is a 6. What is the chance BOTH are 6?
items.why: 11 squares have a 6 in them. Only one of those, 6-6, has two 6s. So it is {answer}, not 1 in 6!

items.q: Two dice are rolled and the total is {t}. What is the chance that one of the dice is a 6?
items.why: There are {given} ways to make {t}, and {fav} of them have a 6.

items.q: Roll 3 dice and add them. Which total comes up more often: 9 or 10?
items.why: 9 can be made {a_fav} ways and 10 can be made {b_fav} ways. The scientist Galileo worked this out about 400 years ago.

items.q: Roll 3 dice and add them. How many of the 216 ways make a total of 10?
items.why: {answer} ways. That is the most of any total, tied with 11.

items.q: Roll 4 dice. Which is more likely: at least one 6, or no 6 at all?
items.why: No 6 at all happens 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = {b_fav} ways out of {total}. At least one 6 wins with {a_fav}. A gambler, the Chevalier de Méré, won money on this bet over 350 years ago.

items.q: Which is more likely: exactly 2 heads when you flip 2 coins, or exactly 2 heads when you flip 4 coins?
items.why: With 2 coins it is 1 in 4. With 4 coins it is 6 in 16, and 6 in 16 is more than 4 in 16.

items.q: Pay 2 coins to roll two dice. If the total is 10 or more, you win {w} coins. Is it a good deal?
items.why: A total of 10 or more comes up 6 ways out of 36, which is 1 in 6. {detail}

items.q: Which is more likely: 5 or more on one 8-sided die, or a total of 5 or more on two 4-sided dice?
items.why: One 8-sided die: 4 in 8, the same as 8 in 16. Two 4-sided dice: 10 in 16. Adding dice makes the middle totals more common.
